seoTitle: Salary to Hourly Calculator - Convert Annual Salary to Hourly Wage
metaDescription: Free salary to hourly calculator. Convert your annual salary to an equivalent hourly rate, daily, weekly, and monthly pay instantly.
intro: Knowing your exact hourly rate gives you powerful insight whether you are comparing a salaried role to freelance work, evaluating overtime pay, or understanding your true per-hour value. Our free Salary to Hourly Calculator instantly converts your annual salary to an hourly wage, along with daily, weekly, and monthly equivalents, making compensation comparisons simple and transparent.
whatIs: A salary to hourly calculator is a conversion tool that divides your annual salary by the total number of working hours in a year to give you your equivalent hourly rate. This is the reverse of the hourly-to-salary calculation. The standard assumption is 2,080 working hours per year (40 hours per week × 52 weeks). You can adjust the hours per week or weeks per year to reflect your actual work schedule.
howToUse: Enter your Annual Salary — your total gross yearly compensation.
Enter Hours per Week — the average hours worked each week (default 40).
Optionally adjust Weeks per Year (default 52 — reduce for unpaid leave).
Click 'Calculate' to see your Hourly Rate, Daily, Weekly, and Monthly pay.
howItWorks: Hourly Rate = Annual Salary ÷ (Hours per Week × Weeks per Year). For a standard full-time employee: Hourly Rate = Annual Salary ÷ 2,080. Daily Rate = Hourly Rate × 8 (for an 8-hour day). Weekly Rate = Hourly Rate × 40. Monthly Rate = Annual Salary ÷ 12.
workedExample: Your annual salary is $62,400. Working 40 hours per week, 52 weeks per year (2,080 hours): Hourly Rate = $62,400 ÷ 2,080 = $30.00 per hour. Daily = $30 × 8 = $240. Weekly = $30 × 40 = $1,200. Monthly = $62,400 ÷ 12 = $5,200.
resultInterpretation: Your hourly rate is the most useful figure for comparing your compensation to freelance or contract roles, which are typically priced per hour. The daily rate is helpful when evaluating day-rate contracts. The weekly and monthly figures are useful for budgeting and understanding your income at different time horizons. All results are gross (before tax) amounts.
useCases: Freelance Comparison: Understand whether your employer's implicit hourly rate is competitive with freelance market rates.
Overtime Calculation: Calculate your standard hourly rate to determine what overtime pay should be (typically 1.5× the hourly rate).
Part-Time Job Evaluation: Compare the hourly rate of a part-time offer against your current full-time hourly equivalent.
Consulting Fee Setting: Use your current employer's implied hourly rate as a baseline for setting consulting fees.
Job Offer Analysis: Convert a salary offer to hourly terms to compare apples-to-apples with hourly-paid positions.
tipsAndLimitations: All results are gross amounts before income tax and other payroll deductions.

Salaried employees often receive benefits (health insurance, retirement contributions, paid leave) not reflected in hourly rate comparisons. When comparing to contract work, add the cost of those benefits to the hourly calculation.
Exempt salaried employees may work more than 40 hours without overtime pay — dividing your salary by your actual hours worked may give a lower effective hourly rate.
In many jurisdictions, freelance or contract workers must charge a higher hourly rate than their salaried equivalent to account for self-employment taxes, unpaid time off, and no employer benefits.

faq.question: How do I convert my annual salary to an hourly rate?
faq.answer: Divide your annual salary by the total hours worked per year. For a standard full-time job (40 hours/week × 52 weeks = 2,080 hours), divide by 2,080.

faq.question: What hourly rate equals a $60,000 annual salary?
faq.answer: $60,000 ÷ 2,080 = $28.85 per hour for a standard 40-hour work week.

faq.question: Do I need to include benefits in the calculation?
faq.answer: The calculator shows base salary converted to an hourly rate. For a complete comparison with contract work, add the monetary value of benefits (health insurance, retirement match, paid leave) to the annual salary before dividing.

faq.question: How is this different from the hourly to salary calculator?
faq.answer: This tool does the reverse: it starts with an annual salary and breaks it down to hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly rates. The hourly to salary calculator starts with an hourly wage and builds up to an annual figure.

cta: Convert your annual salary to an hourly rate instantly and gain clarity on your true compensation!
disclaimer: All figures are gross (pre-tax) estimates. Actual take-home pay will be lower after income taxes and other deductions. Benefits are not included in this calculation.
